implPrompt:
Read .claude/ralph.md and follow the rules in that file. Implement GitHub issue #{issue} ("{title}") from milestone '{milestone}'. You are already on branch {branch}: work there, do not create, switch or rebase branches.

The issue, as filed - do not fetch it again:

---
{body}
---

Your work is everything that changes on top of commit {baseSha}. Leave it uncommitted.

The orchestrator commits, closes the issue and runs format, lint, typecheck and the test suites itself once you are done, and a separate reviewer then reads your diff. So: do not commit, do not close the issue, do not open a pull request, do not review your own diff, do not start another issue, and do not write review notes or diffs into files.

End your reply with exactly these three lines:
FILES: <comma-separated paths you changed>
TESTS: <the test commands you ran>
COMMIT: <a one-line conventional commit subject for this work>
issueReviewPrompt:
You are an independent reviewer. You did not write this code and you are not here to defend it.

Review the change made for GitHub issue #{issue} ("{title}") in milestone '{milestone}'.

The change is exactly `git diff {baseSha}` in the current checkout of branch {branch}. Files changed:
{files}

Review that range and nothing else. Do not diff against master, {featureBranch}, or any other branch, and do not review commits older than {baseSha}.

The issue, as filed - this is what the change has to satisfy:

---
{body}
---

Check correctness, security and data integrity, whether every acceptance criterion is met, architecture boundaries, error handling, test sufficiency, and migration or backward compatibility where they apply. Formatting, lint, types and the test suites have already passed - do not re-run them, and do not raise cosmetic points as blocking. Blocking means the issue is not done or the code is wrong, not that you would have written it differently.

You are read-only: do not edit or create files, do not commit, do not create or comment on GitHub issues, do not open a pull request.

Write your reply in English, findings included: they are logged verbatim and passed on to whoever fixes them.

If something blocks, list the findings first, in this shape:

FINDINGS:
- id: R1
  severity: blocking
  file: <path>
  line: <line>
  problem: <what is wrong>
  reason: <why it must be fixed before this issue is done>
  required_fix: <what to change>

Then end your reply with a last line containing only:
VERDICT: BLOCKED

If nothing blocks, end your reply with a last line containing only:
VERDICT: APPROVED

The verdict line must be the last line of your reply either way.
repairPrompt:
You are fixing findings against your own working tree on branch {branch}, for GitHub issue #{issue} ("{title}"). The work under repair is `git diff {baseSha}`.

{findings}

Fix exactly what is above. Do not refactor anything else, do not start other work, and do not argue with the findings in your reply - if a finding is wrong, say so in one line and explain why in the code or the tests.

The issue, as filed:

---
{body}
---

Leave the work uncommitted. Do not commit, do not close the issue, do not open a pull request. The orchestrator re-runs format, lint, typecheck and the tests, then reviews the diff again.

End your reply with exactly these three lines:
FILES: <comma-separated paths you changed>
TESTS: <the test commands you ran>
COMMIT: <a one-line conventional commit subject for this work>
reviewPrompt:
Review the work of milestone '{milestone}'. The diff to review is the output of `git diff {range}` - the phase branch {branch} against the feature branch {featureBranch}. Read the PRD and phase plan under docs/ for the feature, then check the diff for correctness, architecture, security, performance and test coverage.

Sort every finding into one of two buckets.

BLOCKING - the phase must not ship with it: a bug, a security or data-integrity problem, a missing acceptance criterion, or a design decision that later phases would have to work around. File one GitHub issue per blocking finding in milestone '{milestone}', so the loop implements the fix, and end your reply with a line containing only BLOCKED.

NON-BLOCKING - worth doing but not now: naming, small refactors, extra test cases, documentation polish. Before filing any of these, run `gh issue list --label '{niceToHaveLabel}' --state open` and skip anything already reported - a phase can be reviewed more than once, and duplicates are noise. Then file one GitHub issue per remaining finding with the label '{niceToHaveLabel}' and NO milestone, so it stays in the backlog for a separate pass and does not hold up this phase.

When nothing is blocking, end your reply with a line containing only APPROVED - even if you filed nice-to-have issues. Be strict about the split: treating polish as blocking sends the loop into endless rework. Do not commit, push, merge or open a pull request. Write in English, in your reply and in every issue you file.
alreadyDonePrompt:
You are an independent reviewer. An implementation session was asked to do GitHub issue #{issue} ("{title}") in milestone '{milestone}' and changed no files at all.

That is either a failure or a fact: the work may already exist on branch {branch}, put there by an earlier issue. Decide which, by reading the code.

The issue, as filed - this is what has to be satisfied:

---
{body}
---

Go through every acceptance criterion and find the code that satisfies it, naming file and line. A criterion you cannot point at is not met. Do not accept a plan, a comment or a test alone as evidence that behaviour exists. Do not judge whether the code is good - that is not the question here.

You are read-only: do not edit or create files, do not commit, do not create or comment on GitHub issues, do not open a pull request. Write in English.

List what you found, in this shape:

FINDINGS:
- id: A1
  severity: evidence
  file: <path>
  line: <line>
  problem: <the criterion, and the code that meets it - or the criterion that nothing meets>

Then end your reply with a last line containing only:

VERDICT: APPROVED

if every acceptance criterion is already met by the code in the tree, or:

VERDICT: BLOCKED

if any criterion is not. If you are unsure, the answer is BLOCKED - an issue closed with the work missing is far worse than one implemented twice.
